premises.text: Status and project communications full of business information stay trapped in person-to-person email, so decisions are worse, work is duplicated, and companies lose money
premises.evidence_span: these communications that are loaded with valuable business information are sent by email from one person to another, and the rest of the company can't access them

premises.text: Managers can set who reports, when, and what template in about 30 seconds, with automated prompting so managers need not chase writers
premises.evidence_span: who you want status reports from, when you want them, and what information they should include

premises.text: Status reports are shared across the team and projects can be followed like a social feed, with a managed recipient list
premises.evidence_span: They're shared among all the people on their team

premises.text: Searching across company status reports reveals people-project relationships and expertise that would otherwise stay in inboxes
premises.evidence_span: we're mapping the relationships between people and projects in a company

value.text: People across the organization understand the whole puzzle so they can align people and resources
value.evidence_span: making status reports more accessible, by making them more consistent, and more powerful to align people and resources across an organization

causal_links.evidence_span: when you look at them across an entire company, you can start to map the relationships between people and projects
decisions are less informed, work is duplicated, and ultimately, companies lose money
status reports are more consistent than they've ever been
each person understanding the entire puzzle and where their pieces fit in
